mechanism_narrative: A sustained recovery in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT mobility indicates a return to pre-pandemic commuting and daily routines, which will directly translate into increased footfall and spending in retail and recreation venues, driving RETAIL_REC higher over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than over the last 28 days despite WORKPLACES and TRANSIT continuing their upward trend.

mechanism_narrative: The sharp week-on-week decline in PARKS mobility suggests a shift away from outdoor leisure activities, potentially re-allocating discretionary time and spending towards indoor retail and recreation, leading to an increase in RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls by more than 15 points week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC decreases or remains flat in the two weeks following a week-on-week PARKS drop greater than 15 points.

mechanism_narrative: The concurrent increase in WORKPLACES mobility and decrease in RESIDENTIAL mobility signifies a broad societal return to out-of-home activities, creating more opportunities for engagement with retail and recreation services, thus boosting RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than over the last 28 days even as WORKPLACES increases and RESIDENTIAL decreases.

mechanism_narrative: A consistent trend of decreasing RESIDENTIAL mobility reflects a sustained reduction in stay-at-home behavior, indicating a broader societal shift towards engaging with the urban environment, which will directly increase RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than over the last 28 days despite RESIDENTIAL mobility continuing its downward trend.

mechanism_narrative: The sudden week-on-week drop in GROCERY_PHARM mobility, following a period of recovery, suggests a potential re-emergence of public caution or localized disruption, which would immediately deter discretionary spending and cause RETAIL_REC to decline in the next week.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM falls by more than 4 points week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC continues to improve in the week following a week-on-week GROCERY_PHARM drop greater than 4 points.

mechanism_narrative: If both PARKS and GROCERY_PHARM mobility experience significant week-on-week declines, it signals a widespread retreat from public spaces due to renewed concerns or restrictions, which will collectively suppress all non-essential out-of-home activities, causing RETAIL_REC to fall over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS and GROCERY_PHARM both fall by more than 4 points week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases or remains flat in the two weeks following simultaneous week-on-week drops of more than 4 points in both PARKS and GROCERY_PHARM.

mechanism_narrative: The steady week-on-week improvement in TRANSIT mobility indicates a growing comfort with and reliance on public transportation, which directly facilitates access to and engagement with retail and recreation destinations, leading to an increase in RETAIL_REC over the next week.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC declines or remains flat in the next week despite TRANSIT mobility continuing its upward trend.

mechanism_narrative: In a reopening environment, if the week-on-week improvement in RETAIL_REC significantly slows down while WORKPLACES mobility continues its upward trend, it indicates that the initial pent-up demand for retail and recreation is being satisfied, leading to a deceleration or even reversal of RETAIL_REC growth over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: RETAIL_REC week-on-week change is less than 2 points while WORKPLACES week-on-week change is greater than 1 point
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC accelerates its improvement over the next 28 days even if its week-on-week growth is less than 2 points while WORKPLACES growth is greater than 1 point.
